chunks: And from him, from Ibrahim, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
And preferably, you hasten the prayer and combine them [Dhuhr and Asr, Fajr and Maghrib, Isha and Fajr] to free your soul for supplication, for it is a day of supplication and asking.
Then you come to the standing place [of Arafat], and upon you should be calmness and dignity, so praise Allah, glorify Him, magnify Him, extol Him, and declare Him Great one hundred times.
And praise Him one hundred times, and glorify Him one hundred times, and recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' one hundred times.
And choose for yourself from supplication whatever you like, and strive [in it], for it is a day of supplication and asking.
And seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan, for the Satan will not distract you in any place more dear to him than that he distract you in that place.
And beware of being occupied with looking at people, and turn your attention to yourself.
And let it be among what you say: 'O Allah, I am Your servant, so do not make me from the most deluded of Your guests, and have mercy on my journey to You from the deep valley.'

And let it be among what you say: 'O Allah, Lord of all the stations, free my neck from the Fire, and broaden for me from Your lawful provision, and ward off from me the evil of the wicked of the jinn and humans.'
And you say: 'O Allah, do not scheme against me, and do not deceive me, and do not gradually lead me [to ruin].'

And you say: 'O Allah, I ask You by Your power, Your generosity, Your nobility, Your bounty, and Your favor, O Most Hearing of the hearers, O Most Seeing of the seers, O Quickest of the Reckoners, O Most Merciful of the merciful.'
That You send prayer upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and that You do for me such and such.

And let it be among what you say, while you are raising your head to the sky: 'O Allah, my need to You is that if You give it to me, what You withhold from me will not harm me, and if You withhold it from me, what You give me will not benefit me.'
I ask You for the deliverance of my neck from the Fire.
And let it be among what you say: 'O Allah, I am Your servant, and the possession of Your hand, my forelock is in Your hand, and my term is by Your knowledge.'

I ask You to enable me for that which pleases You about me, and to accept from me the rituals which You showed Your friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and pointed out to Your prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).
And let it be among what you say: 'O Allah, make me from those whose work You were pleased with, whose life You prolonged, and whom You gave life after death a good life.'
And it is recommended that one seek deliverance on the evening of Arafat through freeing slaves and giving charity.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, the One (Quranic Surah)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette and specific supplication for the Day of Arafat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the spiritual protocol for the Day of Arafat, emphasizing the strategic combination of prayer and supplication to maximize divine acceptance. It prescribes specific dhikr and introspective du'as, highlighting the Prophet’s tradition of seeking deliverance from Hell and the acceptance of Hajj rituals through humble submission. The text underscores the psychological discipline required to avoid distraction by Satan during this pivotal moment of standing before God.
